summary:
Aero Kidz: Lunar Outpost is a 3D lunar-base survival game for children, built in Godot 4 with C#. Players explore a Moon outpost as a young astronaut, guided by Nova, a friendly robot. They complete three science missions: growing plants in a hydroponic bio-dome, drilling for samples at a remote site reached by rover, and observing the Sun from a telescope. Each mission includes a hands-on minigame and a real NASA-inspired hazard, such as an oxygen leak, contaminated water or a solar flare. Kids choose between staying safe and gaining more science, while keeping Oxygen, Power and Shield above zero. The solar-flare mission uses live NASA space-weather data (DONKI), so real events shape gameplay. At the end, players board the Apollo 11 Lunar Module to fly home.

The game turns the real challenges of living on the Moon, like life support, energy, radiation and resource trade-offs, into decisions children can understand. It matters because missions like Artemis will depend on a future generation that understands these challenges. Making exploration playable builds curiosity, problem-solving and interest in STEM.
details:
Aero Kidz: Lunar Outpost

*When opening the zip file, the WINDOW PROTECTION might be preventing it from loading*

SOURCE CODE (GITHUB REPO LINK): https://github.com/amandakho2020-stack/nasa-space-app-challenge

What it does: Aero Kidz is a 3D Moon-base game for kids. A friendly robot named Nova guides players through a lunar outpost with oxygen, power and shield rooms, a Bio-Dome, a telescope room and a rover bay. There are three missions:

  • Grow plants: catch water drops to grow and harvest crops.
  • Drill: drive a rover 180 m to a drill site and keep the drill from overheating.
  • Solar storm: observe the Sun and survive a storm shaped by live NASA DONKI space-weather data.

Each mission brings a hazard, like an oxygen leak, contaminated water or a solar flare. Players choose between fixing it safely and taking a risk for more science points. The game ends with a flight home in the Apollo 11 Lunar Module, wrapped in a main menu, intro and outro videos, and a high-score screen.

Benefits and impact: Kids learn life support, power budgets, radiation shielding and low gravity by playing, not by reading. The choices teach the same safety-versus-reward trade-offs real mission planners face. We want to spark STEM curiosity in the generation growing up with Artemis.

Tools:

  • Godot 4.7 (.NET) with C#
  • Imported 3D models (Lunar Module, Spitzer Space Telescope, rover, astronaut)
  • Moon terrain and base interiors generated by code
  • Lunar gravity physics
  • NASA DONKI data
  • Git and GitHub
  • Ordinary Windows PCs
  • Claude Code Opus 5.5 (our main SI usage)

Creativity: Colorful 2D minigames run inside a 3D world. The Moon surface and base are generated by code. The drill site is far enough away that you really need the rover. Real spacecraft and live NASA data tie the game to actual missions.

What we considered:

  • Kid-friendly pacing: Nova shows one message at a time, and floor arrows and “GO HERE” markers show the way.
  • Accessibility: touchpad support, and timers can be turned off.
  • Scientific accuracy: one-sixth gravity, harsh lighting from a sky with no air, and oxygen that only drains outside the base.
  • Reliability: an offline fallback for the NASA data.
  • Performance: runs on ordinary laptops.
  • Teamwork: modular code so teammates could work in parallel.
